note: Historical record. Nothing here feeds the calculation directly - values are transcribed into models.json and hardware.json only after review. Confidence levels: measured (first-party run with pinned build), published (public reproducible recipe), community (unverified report).

benchmarks.config: vLLM main dd72658e / FlashInfer 0.6.15.post1 / TP1 / FP8 KV / NVFP4 weights / no DFlash / 262,144 tokens per agent / 10 concurrent

metrics.label: Peak HBM
metrics.note: 242.8 GiB of 252 GB - saturated, zero spill

benchmarks.qualification: 10/10 exact requests, 10 output hashes verified, zero failures, zero preemptions, zero swap, unique prompts, forced output, no CPU/KV/UVA offload.
caveats: Benchmark conditions, not realistic mixed traffic. Unique prompts mean zero prefix reuse - the worst case for KV, but the best case for throughput consistency.
No realistic-traffic soak exists for this configuration, so it is not directly comparable to the DeepSeek numbers below.

metrics.label: Draft acceptance

benchmarks.qualification: 40-minute soak: 553 requests, 212,974 tokens generated, zero empty completions, zero degenerate output, zero errors, no container restarts. Per-stream held 22.1-22.3 across all eight 5-minute windows.
caveats: Patch 4 is mandatory: without it throughput halves at unchanged output quality, which sends you looking in the wrong place. Root cause is a drafter loader silently dropping twelve shared-expert tensors.
30% cold penalty after boot and after any idle period - first requests run at ~58 instead of ~83 tok/s, and it is not visible in the boot log.
With stream=true you measure steps per second, not tokens per second: 14.7 vs 60.1 on the same request. Read usage.completion_tokens.

benchmarks.model: DeepSeek V4 Flash DSpark, official FP8 (~167 GB)
benchmarks.config: Community vLLM build (upstream fails to load the 0731 release: new MTP norm layout) / dspark k=5 / kv-cache-dtype fp8 / gpu-memory-utilization 0.94 / max-model-len 524,288
benchmarks.qualification: Unverified community report on a non-official build.
caveats: max_num_seqs > 4 fails deterministically on the first request. Root cause is a hardcoded prefill chunk size feeding an empty padding slice into the sparse MLA kernel. This is an implementation defect, not an architectural limit - a production build should not carry it.
Upstream vLLM does not load this release at all, so the build under test is not what you would run in production.
confidence_head is fully wired in this build but defaults to a threshold of 0, i.e. present and unused.
OPEN INCONSISTENCY: the KV per token implied here (~10.6 KB with FP8 KV) contradicts the DGX Spark recipe (~27 KB with NVFP4 KV). NVFP4 should be more compact, not double.
OPEN INCONSISTENCY: 167 GB across 284 billion declared parameters is 0.588 bytes per parameter, so not pure FP8. Either the checkpoint is mixed, or the 284B figure does not describe this variant.
benchmarks.highlight: The most interesting result is a non-result: the author expected an SM120 kernel wall and never hit one. Measured efficiency is around 28.5% against the 6% this tool assumes conservatively for that column.
